text:
maya.r: stuck on the quickstart. followed README, set REDWOOD_API_KEY and REDWOOD_WORKSPACE_ID, but first call returns 403 org_billing_missing. any known gotchas?
jon.s: which quickstart did you run (node/python) and did you use the sample repo's .env or your own?
maya.r: node quickstart, i copied values from console into my .env and restarted the sample. curl yields: 
```
HTTP/2 403
{"error":"org_billing_missing: workspace requires billing setup"}
```
jon.s: that error usually means the workspace you're hitting is flagged trial/unpaid. double-check the workspace id in the console is the same string you exported, and confirm the API key belongs to that workspace. also check for cached creds in ~/.redwood/credentials.json.
maya.r: i didn't know about that cache. i have an old CLI install from months ago. checking ~/.redwood... yep it exists and contains a different workspace id.
jon.s: SDK/CLI will prefer cached creds over env, which is surprising. we should add a note in the quickstart. can you clear the file and retry?
maya.r: removed it, restarted sample, still 403. this time the error payload includes a link: https://redwood.ai/docs/onboarding#billing but the link isn't in the quickstart troubleshooting.
jon.s: hm. devex-bot, can you dump the workspace state for both ids?
devex-bot: workspace ws_personal_dev: status=trial, billing_info=missing. workspace ws_old_test: status=disabled, billing_info=missing, notes=auto-created-by-cli. docs: https://redwood.ai/docs/onboarding#billing
maya.r: i switched REDWOOD_WORKSPACE_ID to the personal dev one and created a new API key scoped to that workspace. still 403.
jon.s: what's the API key format? service keys start with sk_ and personal keys start with pk_. If you created the key in the org panel it may be tied to org workspaces only.
maya.r: my key is sk_live_abc123. created a new key under my user -> API keys and now it's sk_dev_987. retried and finally got 200: {"id":"gen_1","status":"ok","text":"hey"}
maya.r: so it was a combination of cached creds + key scoping that made debugging confusing. spent an hour on this.
jon.s: thanks for the details. action items: (1) add a troubleshooting note to quickstart about credential precedence: env > cache? wait, actually SDK prefers cache over env, so we need to fix docs and maybe the precedence logic, (2) SDK should surface structured machine-readable error codes like {"code":"billing_required","help": "https://redwood.ai/docs/onboarding#billing"}, (3) quickstart should show how to list workspaces and create a personal dev workspace for test calls.
maya.r: filed a tiny doc patch with the cache note and a repro snippet.
jon.s: created ticket RED-DEVEX-478 to change the error payload and RED-DEVEX-479 to evaluate credential precedence. ci-bot: queued job to run quickstart smoke tests to surface this earlier.
maya.r: thanks all. leaving a short checklist for the docs: - check ~/.redwood/credentials.json - confirm API key was created under the expected workspace - prefer user-scoped key for personal dev workspace - use --noproxy to rule out header rewriting
jon.s: will include that. closing thread once docs PR lands. :rocket:
